subtype: Approach: planning what to do if she forgets a line [Thinking]
passage: I'm Omkar, and I was in the audience during rehearsal when Parveen stopped mid-scene, looking worried. She turned to the teacher afterwards. "What if I forget my line on the day?" The teacher did not say 'you won't'. Instead they sat on the stage steps and made a plan together. If Parveen forgets, she pauses, takes a slow breath, and looks at Tara, who says the next line. Parveen repeated it twice, then practised it, even pretending to forget a line so she could try the pause. During the show she did forget, once, and it worked: the pause was so short that most people never noticed.

qa.q: Who says the next line if Parveen forgets?
What was Parveen worried about after the rehearsal?
qa.a: Parveen worried about forgetting her line on the day, and wanted a plan for it.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Parveen use as well, and why?
qa.a: Parveen could keep a small cue word in mind or practise the line with friends until it is automatic. More than one safety net gives even more calm.

qa.q: How does Omkar see the plan?
qa.a: Omkar watched from the audience and saw the pause work, so Omkar probably feels impressed by how a small plan kept the show moving.

grounding: A girl asks what if she forgets and plans with her teacher to pause, breathe and look at Tara who has the next line, seen by an observer.
